_comment: Class-level interaction rules. Each rule expands to (members of class_a) x (members of class_b) pairs. Checked ONLY when no explicit pair exists in drug_interactions.json, so curated entries always win.

rules.reason: NSAIDs impair platelet function and irritate the gastric lining. Combined with an anticoagulant, the risk of gastrointestinal and other bleeding rises substantially.
rules.recommendation: Avoid the combination. Paracetamol is the usual alternative for pain or fever.

rules.reason: Two agents both affecting platelet function and gastric mucosa markedly increase bleeding and ulcer risk.
rules.recommendation: Review with the prescriber; consider gastric protection or paracetamol instead.

rules.reason: NSAIDs reduce the blood-pressure-lowering effect and, together with an ACE inhibitor, cut blood flow to the kidneys.
rules.recommendation: Avoid regular NSAID use; monitor blood pressure and kidney function if unavoidable.

rules.reason: NSAIDs blunt the antihypertensive effect and add renal strain when combined with an ARB.
rules.recommendation: Prefer paracetamol. Short NSAID courses only, with monitoring.

rules.reason: NSAIDs reduce diuretic effectiveness and add kidney strain. With an ACE inhibitor or ARB as well this becomes the high-risk 'triple whammy'.
rules.recommendation: Check whether the patient is also on an ACE inhibitor or ARB, and monitor renal function.

rules.reason: NSAIDs reduce the antihypertensive effect of thiazides and may impair renal function.
rules.recommendation: Monitor blood pressure; consider paracetamol.

rules.reason: Combining an NSAID with a steroid substantially raises the risk of peptic ulceration and gastrointestinal bleeding.
rules.recommendation: Consider gastric protection or an alternative analgesic.

rules.reason: SSRIs reduce platelet serotonin and, with an NSAID, increase upper gastrointestinal bleeding risk.
rules.recommendation: Consider a proton pump inhibitor or paracetamol instead.

rules.reason: NSAIDs reduce renal clearance of methotrexate and related agents, raising the risk of bone-marrow and kidney toxicity.
rules.recommendation: Avoid unless specifically sanctioned and monitored by the prescriber.

rules.reason: Two different blood-thinning mechanisms combined substantially increase bleeding risk.
rules.recommendation: Confirm the combination is deliberate, time-limited and monitored.

rules.reason: Azole antifungals inhibit anticoagulant metabolism, raising drug levels and INR.
rules.recommendation: Avoid if possible; otherwise close INR monitoring is required.

rules.reason: Fluoroquinolones can potentiate anticoagulant effect and raise INR.
rules.recommendation: Request INR monitoring or select an alternative antibiotic.

rules.reason: Macrolides can increase anticoagulant effect through enzyme inhibition.
rules.recommendation: Consider an INR check during and shortly after the antibiotic course.

rules.reason: SSRIs impair platelet aggregation, adding to anticoagulant bleeding risk.
rules.recommendation: Counsel the patient on bleeding signs; review with the prescriber.

rules.reason: Enzyme inducers accelerate anticoagulant breakdown, reducing its effect and risking clot formation.
rules.recommendation: Dose adjustment with close INR monitoring is required.

rules.reason: Both retain potassium. Combined use can cause dangerous hyperkalaemia and cardiac arrhythmia.
rules.recommendation: Serum potassium and renal function monitoring required.

rules.reason: Both raise serum potassium; together they risk hyperkalaemia.
rules.recommendation: Monitor potassium and renal function.

rules.reason: An ACE inhibitor already retains potassium; adding a supplement can cause hyperkalaemia.
rules.recommendation: Confirm with the prescriber and check serum potassium.

rules.reason: An ARB already retains potassium; a supplement compounds the risk.
rules.recommendation: Confirm with the prescriber and check serum potassium.

rules.reason: Dual blockade of the renin-angiotensin system increases the risk of hyperkalaemia, hypotension and acute kidney injury without added benefit for most patients.
rules.recommendation: This combination is generally not recommended; confirm with the prescriber.

rules.reason: Macrolides inhibit statin metabolism, raising statin levels and the risk of muscle injury including rhabdomyolysis.
rules.recommendation: Pause the statin during the antibiotic course or select a different antibiotic.

rules.reason: Azole antifungals sharply raise statin exposure, increasing myopathy risk.
rules.recommendation: Avoid the combination or temporarily withhold the statin.

rules.reason: Both affect muscle tissue; combined use raises the risk of rhabdomyolysis.
rules.recommendation: Avoid; a safer lipid-lowering combination should be considered.

rules.reason: Verapamil and diltiazem raise statin levels through enzyme inhibition.
rules.recommendation: Dose limits apply for some statins; confirm the prescribed dose.

rules.reason: Both dilate blood vessels. Together they can cause a sudden, severe and potentially fatal drop in blood pressure.
rules.recommendation: This combination is contraindicated. Do not dispense without clinician review.

rules.reason: Tramadol and related opioids raise serotonin levels; combined with an SSRI this can trigger serotonin syndrome.
rules.recommendation: Review with the prescriber. Watch for agitation, tremor, sweating and fever.

rules.reason: Two serotonergic antidepressants together carry a high risk of serotonin syndrome.
rules.recommendation: Confirm this is a deliberate, supervised cross-taper.

rules.reason: Both increase serotonergic activity, with a risk of serotonin syndrome.
rules.recommendation: Counsel the patient on warning symptoms; review if both are long-term.

rules.reason: Combined serotonergic effect raises the risk of serotonin syndrome.
rules.recommendation: Review with the prescriber before dispensing.

rules.reason: Both depress the central nervous system. Together they significantly increase the risk of profound sedation and respiratory depression.
rules.recommendation: Avoid where possible. If unavoidable, use the lowest doses and counsel on sedation risk.

rules.reason: Additive central nervous system depression with risk of respiratory compromise.
rules.recommendation: Avoid the combination; review with the prescriber.

rules.reason: Two sedative-hypnotics together cause excessive sedation, confusion and fall risk.
rules.recommendation: Duplicate sedative therapy; confirm only one is intended.

rules.reason: Azole antifungals raise sulfonylurea levels, increasing the risk of hypoglycaemia.
rules.recommendation: Advise blood-glucose monitoring during the antifungal course.

rules.reason: Beta blockers can mask the adrenergic warning signs of low blood sugar such as tremor and palpitations.
rules.recommendation: Counsel the patient on recognising hypoglycaemia without these cues.

rules.reason: Cotrimoxazole and related agents can potentiate sulfonylureas and cause hypoglycaemia.
rules.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose during treatment.

rules.reason: Two medicines that each prolong the cardiac QT interval, taken together, increase the risk of a dangerous arrhythmia called torsades de pointes.
rules.recommendation: Avoid the combination or arrange ECG and electrolyte monitoring.

rules.reason: Additive slowing of heart rate and cardiac conduction can cause bradycardia or heart block.
rules.recommendation: Monitor heart rate; confirm the combination is intended.

rules.reason: Verapamil or diltiazem with a beta blocker can cause severe bradycardia, heart block and heart failure.
rules.recommendation: Generally avoided; requires specialist review.

rules.reason: Calcium and iron bind thyroid hormone in the gut and substantially reduce its absorption.
rules.recommendation: Separate the doses by at least four hours.

rules.reason: Reduced gastric acid impairs levothyroxine absorption, which may reduce thyroid control.
rules.recommendation: Monitor thyroid function if both are long-term.

rules.reason: Calcium, iron, magnesium and aluminium bind the antibiotic in the gut and markedly reduce its absorption, risking treatment failure.
rules.recommendation: Separate doses by at least two hours before or six hours after the antibiotic.

rules.reason: Mineral chelation greatly reduces tetracycline absorption.
rules.recommendation: Separate the doses by at least two hours.

rules.reason: Fluoroquinolones raise theophylline levels, which can cause seizures and cardiac arrhythmia.
rules.recommendation: Avoid; select an alternative antibiotic.

rules.reason: Macrolides can raise theophylline levels towards the toxic range.
rules.recommendation: Monitor for nausea, tremor and palpitations.

rules.reason: Some proton pump inhibitors, particularly omeprazole, reduce the activation of clopidogrel and may lessen its antiplatelet effect.
rules.recommendation: Pantoprazole is generally the preferred acid-suppressing agent.

rules.reason: Azole antifungals sharply raise levels of ciclosporin, tacrolimus and related agents, risking toxicity.
rules.recommendation: Requires specialist dose adjustment and level monitoring.

rules.reason: Enzyme inducers lower immunosuppressant levels and risk transplant rejection or disease flare.
rules.recommendation: Specialist review with drug level monitoring.

rules.reason: Enzyme inducers reduce statin levels and may lessen cholesterol control.
rules.recommendation: Monitor lipid profile; dose adjustment may be needed.

rules.reason: Both lower serum potassium; combined use can cause hypokalaemia.
rules.recommendation: Monitor potassium, particularly in patients also taking digoxin.

rules.reason: Diuretic-induced dehydration reduces renal clearance of metformin, raising the risk of lactic acidosis.
rules.recommendation: Ensure adequate hydration; periodic renal function checks.

rules.reason: Both increase fluid loss. Combined use raises the risk of dehydration, low blood pressure and kidney injury, particularly in older patients.
rules.recommendation: Counsel on hydration; monitor blood pressure and renal function.

rules.reason: Sedating antihistamines add to benzodiazepine drowsiness, increasing falls and impaired alertness.
rules.recommendation: Advise against driving; consider a non-sedating antihistamine.
